item.title: Former Flying Fijians prop Campese Ma'afu joins Fijian Drua as scrum coach
item.description: Former Flying Fijians prop Campese Ma'afu has joined the Swire Shipping Fijian Drua as their scrum coach. He says finally he gets to be onboard with the Fijian Drua and it has been a long time coming
item.content:encoded:
Former Flying Fijians prop Campese Ma'afu has joined the Swire Shipping Fijian Drua as their scrum coach.

He says finally he gets to be onboard with the Fijian Drua and it has been a long time coming

The former prop says he is so excited to be in Fiji with his family, who have come for two weeks to help him set up for the new journey.

Ma'afu who has played 62 Tests for Fiji made his debut in June 2010, where he squared up against older brother Salesi.

The Fijian Drua will take on the Highlanders in their first game on Saturday 13th February, with the venue yet to be confirmed.

item.title: Wearing the Fiji Bati jersey is about more than rugby – Turuva
item.description: Vodafone Fiji Bati winger Sunia Turuva says wearing the Bati jersey is a reminder that he is not just playing for himself and his family, but also representing Fijians at home and around the world. He says representing Fiji has been a humbling experience, knowing that young players back home dream of having the same opportunity.
item.content:encoded:
Vodafone Fiji Bati winger Sunia Turuva says wearing the Bati jersey is a reminder that he is not just playing for himself and his family, but also representing Fijians at home and around the world.

He says representing Fiji has been a humbling experience, knowing that young players back home dream of having the same opportunity.

Turuva debuted for the Bati in 2022 before playing his first NRL game, something he had not expected when setting his goals at the beginning of that year.

The winger says his original goal was simply to make the Fiji squad and travel to the Rugby League World Cup, but he was selected for the mid-year Test and given the opportunity to represent his country earlier than expected.

He says sharing the news with his family was a special moment, particularly as his older brother was excited to tell everyone about his selection.

Turuva says the strong bond within the Bati camp also makes representing his country different from playing at club level.

He says the players begin and end each day with devotions and spend much of their free time together drinking tea, playing the guitar and singing Fijian hymns.

Turuva says these moments strengthen the bond between the players and remind them of the responsibility t hat comes with wearing the Fiji jersey.

He says knowing that Fijians around the world are watching motivates the players to give their best and never take the opportunity to represent their country for granted.

Turuva has been named in the Fiji Bati squad for their Rugby League World Cup campaign.

The Bati will begin their World Cup campaign against the Cook Islands at 5.05pm this Sunday at McDonald Jones Stadium in Newcastle.

They will then face Australia at 9.05pm on the 25th of this month before taking on New Zealand at 4.30pm on the 31st.

item.title: Australia edge New Zealand 24-22 in thrilling Rugby League World Cup opener
item.description: Australian captain Isaah Yeo says the 2026 Rugby League World Cup feels different, after leading the Kangaroos to a thrilling 24-22 victory over New Zealand in the tournament opener in Sydney last night. The match, played before a crowd of 41,255 , delivered spectacular tries, strong defence and a dramatic finish as Australia secured the win through debutant Jack Bostock, who scored a hat-trick, i
item.content:encoded:
Australian captain Isaah Yeo says the 2026 Rugby League World Cup feels different, after leading the Kangaroos to a thrilling 24-22 victory over New Zealand in the tournament opener in Sydney last night.

The match, played before a crowd of 41,255 , delivered spectacular tries, strong defence and a dramatic finish as Australia secured the win through debutant Jack Bostock, who scored a hat-trick, including the decisive try in the closing minutes.

Yeo says the atmosphere and growing interest surrounding this year's tournament reflect the excitement building around international rugby league.

He says the attention surrounding the competition has also felt different compared with the previous World Cup, which was held in England.

The crowd of 41,255 was Sydney's largest for a Test match in more than 50 years, since 55,505 fans attended the deciding match of the 1974 Ashes series between Australia and Great Britain at the Sydney Cricket Ground.

It was also the city's biggest World Cup attendance since the 1968 final between Australia and France.

New Zealand captain James Fisher-Harris also praised the atmosphere, describing it as one of the best he had experienced in an Australia-New Zealand clash.

Australia coach Kevin Walters said the match was one of the best he had watched in a long time, praising the intensity between the two rivals.

He said Australia would take confidence from the win but expected another tough contest when the sides meet again.

New Zealand coach Stacey Jones remained optimistic about his team's chances despite the narrow defeat and the loss of star full-back Kalyn Ponga, who scored two tries before leaving the field with a reported broken arm .

Jones said there were positives to take from the performance, although the team would need to make adjustment s as the tournament progressed.

He said New Zealand would learn from the defeat and work to improve without making major changes.

Meanwhile, t he Bati will begin their World Cup campaign against the Cook Islands at 5.05pm this Sunday at McDonald Jones Stadium in Newcastle.

They will then face Australia at 9.05pm on the 25th of this month before taking on New Zealand at 4.30pm on the 31st.

item.title: Family support keeps Daunivalu motivated ahead of Youth Olympic Games
item.description: 15-year-old basketball player Nyssa Daunivalu says the support of her family helps her overcome difficult moments as she prepares to represent Fiji at the 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, Senegal. Originally from Gau, the St Joseph's Secondary School student says she sometimes feels demoralised after a bad game or training session.
item.content:encoded:
15-year-old basketball player Nyssa Daunivalu says the support of her family helps her overcome difficult moments as she prepares to represent Fiji at the 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, Senegal.

Originally from Gau, the St Joseph's Secondary School student says she sometimes feels demoralised after a bad game or training session.

She says the support and encouragement of her family helps her overcome these challenges and stay motivated to keep improving as a player.

Daunivalu says preparations for the Games are going well, with the team working hard and building on the chemistry developed during last years Under-17 Championship in Newcastle.

She says the players are familiar with one anothers playing styles, which has helped them work well together.

The 15-year-old also balances her basketball commitments with schoolwork by setting aside two hours to study after school before attending training.

Daunivalu has thanked those supporting her journey and encouraged other young people who dream of playing basketball to keep working hard and pursuing their goals.

The 2026 Youth Olympic Games will be held in Dakar, Senegal, from October 30 to November 13.

item.title: Ikanivere to Captain the Flying Fijians against Japan
item.description: Tevita Ikanivere will Captain the FIJI Water Flying Fijians as they prepare for the Japan Centennial Test under the guidance of their new head coach, South African Jake White, who led the Springboks to victory at the 2007 Rugby World Cup. item.content:encoded:
Tevita Ikanivere will Captain the FIJI Water Flying Fijians as they prepare for the Japan Centennial Test under the guidance of their new head coach, South African Jake White, who led the Springboks to victory at the 2007 Rugby World Cup.

Ikanivere, who has been a key figure in Fiji’s forward pack, will play a central role in the team’s preparations as they look to deliver a strong performance against Japan.

The squad features experienced forwards Peni Ravai, Mesake Doge, Samuela Tawake, Isoa Nasilasila, Mesake Vocevoce and Motikiai Murray, who are expected to provide strength, physicality and leadership up front.

They will be supported by Kitione Salawa, Isoa Tuwai, Meli Tuni, Penaia Cakobau and Kavaia Tagivetaua, adding depth and competition within the forward pack.

In the backs, Frank Lomani, Ben Volavola, Sam Wye, Kemu Valetini and Isaiah Armstrong-Ravula are among the players expected to play important roles in directing Fiji’s attack.

The squad also includes experienced campaigners Terio Tamani, Joji Nasova, Isikeli Rabitu and Maleli Nauvasi as the Flying Fijians look to combine attacking flair with composure and consistency.

Meanwhile, the selection provides opportunities for emerging players to make their mark on the international stage, with several players identified as potential debutants in the squad announcement.

The inclusion of new talent alongside established internationals reflects the team's efforts to build depth and strengthen competition for places within the national side.

The Flying Fijians will be looking to put their preparations into action against Japan , with the Test providing an important opportunity to assess the squad ahead of their upcoming international commitments.

Fiji will face Japan next Saturday at 5.50pm.
